newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Mother, baby found dead in Venezuela quake ruin.
newsitem.headline: Mother, baby found dead in Venezuela quake ruin.

text.p: Rescuers sifting through the ruins of a collapsed building found the decomposed bodies of a mother and her baby on Monday, taking to 76 the death toll from last week's Venezuelan earthquake, Civil Defence officials said.
The 27-year-old woman and her year-old baby girl were pulled from beneath the mound of rubble that was once an eight-story office and apartment block in Cumana, 255 miles (410 km) east of Caracas.
Another seven people were thought to be buried in the ruins.
"We keep looking but everything seems to indicate that they are dead," a firemen working at the site said.

In addition to the deaths, more than 500 people were injured in Wednesday's quake, which measured at 6.9 on the Richter scale. Many of the dead were children crushed in their classrooms as they took end-of-term exams.
Seismological technicians said on Monday that more than 700 aftershocks had been recorded since the first tremor and seismic activity could continue for several months.

In Cariaco, 40 miles (60 km) east of Cumana, residents were vaccinated against cholera. The small agricultural town, which bore the brunt of the quake, remains without running water and electricity and more than 500 families are living in tents and temporary accommodation.
